    ** dx₄/dt = ic **

The principle is a *physical principle*, not a mathematical postulate or axiom. ## Physical Foundation: The McGucken Principle

### The Principle

**Principle (McGucken Principle).** The fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every spacetime event:

    dx₄/dt = ic.

This is a *physical principle*, not a mathematical axiom or notational convenience. The fourth dimension is the physical, dynamical, geometric direction that expands at c from every spacetime event. The imaginary unit i is the algebraic marker for the orthogonality of x₄ to the three spatial dimensions x₁, x₂, x₃: the same i whose square gives the Lorentzian sign (ict)² = -c² t².

Integration of (eq:mcg) with the source-origin convention x₄(0) = 0 gives Minkowski's coordinate form:

    x₄ = ic t.

The mathematical relation between (eq:mcg) and (eq:integrated) is one calculus operation in either direction. The physical content is asymmetric: (eq:mcg) is the dynamical statement of an actual physical motion of x₄; (eq:integrated) is the integrated kinematic shadow of that motion at coordinate time t. The textbook tradition has worked with the integrated shadow since 1908 without recognizing the dynamical reality it shadows. Recovering the physical content is the foundation of every chain of theorems in this paper.

## Co-Generation Theorem: (ℳ_G, D_M) from One Principle

**Theorem (Space--Operator Co-Generation).** **[Grade 1]**.
The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic generates simultaneously the McGucken Space ℳ_G and the McGucken Operator D_M:

    ** dx₄/dt = ic  ⇒  (ℳ_G, D_M). **

The same primitive physical law generates the source-arena and the source-operator together, as a single co-generated source-pair.

*Proof.* The principle integrates to x₄ = ic t under the source-origin convention x₄(0) = 0. Define

    Φ_M(t, x₄)  :=  x₄ - ic t.

Then Φ_M(t, x₄) = 0 ⇔ x₄ = ic t, so the McGucken Principle is precisely the constraint Φ_M = 0. The four-coordinate Euclidean carrier E₄ with coordinates (x₁, x₂, x₃, x₄) supplies the ambient set; together with Φ_M this defines a structured arena.

The directional derivative along the integral curve x₄ = ic t is, by the chain rule,

    (d)/(dt)|_M  =  ∂_t + (dx₄)/(dt) ∂_{x₄}  =  ∂_t + ic ∂_{x₄}.

Therefore the McGucken Operator

    D_M  :=  ∂_t + ic ∂_{x₄}

is the differential expression of the same physical law that defines Φ_M. By direct computation, D_M Φ_M = ∂_t Φ_M + ic ∂_{x₄}Φ_M = -ic + ic · 1 = 0, so D_M is tangent to the McGucken hypersurface and preserves it.

The spherical wavefront structure Σ_M at any event p is the locus

    Σ_M(p, t)  :=  \{ q : dist(p, q) = c t \},

with isotropy under the spatial rotation group SO(3) acting at p. This sphere is the geometric content of the principle's spherical-symmetry clause: the principle states that x₄ expands isotropically in three-space, and Σ_M is the surface reached by that expansion in coordinate time t.

The structured arena

    ℳ_G  :=  (E₄,  Φ_M,  D_M,  Σ_M)

is therefore generated by the McGucken Principle alone, and the operator D_M is co-generated as the principle's directional derivative.  ∎

**Remark (Status of Σ_M).** Σ_M is included in the source-pair signature for emphasis: the McGucken Sphere is the geometric atom of spacetime in the McGucken framework, and its presence as a labeled component of ℳ_G records the spherical-symmetry content of dx₄/dt = ic. Strictly, once the Lorentzian metric is induced (Theorem~(thm:lorentzproj)), the null hypersurface \{ q : ds²(p,q) = 0 \} is a theorem of the metric; the sphere Σ_M is the spatial-slice cross-section of that null hypersurface. The framework can therefore be presented in either form: as (E₄, Φ_M, D_M, Σ_M) with Σ_M primitive, or as (E₄, Φ_M, D_M) with Σ_M derived. Both presentations are equivalent. We retain the four-tuple form following [mcguckenSpace2026] for explicitness about the spherical-symmetry content.

### Why this is structurally novel

Standard mathematical physics follows the architectural pattern

    arena  →  structure  →  operator  →  dynamics,

in which each level is supplied as separate primitive data. General relativity supplies a Lorentzian manifold (M, g), defines the Levi-Civita connection ∇, and writes the Einstein field equations. Quantum mechanics supplies a separable Hilbert space ℋ, defines self-adjoint operators on ℋ, and writes the Schr\"odinger equation. In every case the operator must differentiate something defined somewhere; the arena precedes the operator.

The McGucken framework collapses this four-stage architecture onto the four constituents of a single source-relation:

The four-fold collapse is read directly off the equation. The source-pair (ℳ_G, D_M) packages the four constituents as 2+2: ℳ_G carries the arena and structure (dx₄ and i), D_M carries the operator and dynamics (d/dt and c).

## Lorentzian Projection and the Master Equation

The first physical structure derived from (ℳ_G, D_M) is Lorentzian spacetime itself.

**Theorem (Lorentzian Projection).** **[Grade 1]**.
The McGucken constraint Φ_M = 0 projects E₄ to Lorentzian spacetime M_{1,3} with induced interval

    ds²  =  dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² - c² dt².

*Proof.* The four-coordinate Euclidean interval is

    dℓ²  =  dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² + dx₄².

On the constraint surface x₄ = ic t, the differential gives dx₄ = ic dt, so

    dx₄²  =  (ic dt)²  =  -c² dt².

Substituting yields (eq:minkowski). The Lorentzian signature is the algebraic shadow of the imaginary character of x₄; the minus sign records orthogonality, not unreality.  ∎

**Theorem (Master Equation).** **[Grade 1]**.
The four-velocity u^μ = dx^μ/dτ of any particle satisfies

    u^μ u_μ  =  -c²

in Minkowski signature (-, +, +, +). Equivalently, the four-velocity budget

    |(dx₄)/(dτ)|² + |(d**x**)/(dτ)|²  =  c².

*Proof.* Proper time is defined by dτ² = -(1/c²) g_{μν} dx^μ dx^ν. With u^μ = dx^μ/dτ and components u⁰ = cγ, u^j = v^jγ where γ = 1/√(1 - v²/c²):

    u^μ u_μ = -(cγ)² + (vγ)² = -c²γ²(1 - v²/c²) = -c².

The identification u₄ = du₄/dτ = icγ in the McGucken numbering follows from x₄ = ict by chain rule. The budget (eq:budget) follows by writing u^μ u_μ = -c² in components.  ∎

**Theorem (McGucken-Invariance Lemma).** **[Grade 1]**.
The rate of x₄'s expansion is gravitationally invariant: dx₄/dt = ic holds globally on the four-manifold M, with ∂(dx₄/dt)/∂ g_{μν} = 0 for all metric components. Only the spatial dimensions x₁, x₂, x₃ curve under mass-energy.

*Proof.* The principle states dx₄/dt = ic at every spacetime event with c a fundamental constant. The only quantities in this equation are dx₄, dt, i, c --- none of which is a metric component. Therefore the equation depends on no metric component, and ∂(dx₄/dt)/∂ g_{μν} = 0 trivially. Equivalently, x₄'s rate is invariant under arbitrary smooth changes of the spatial metric h_{ij}. The result is forced by the principle alone.  ∎

**Corollary (Doctrine: Spatial slices curve, x₄ is invariant).** Gravitational time dilation is a feature of the spatial-slice metric, not of x₄'s rate. Gravitational redshift is a feature of light propagation through curved spatial geometry. There is no graviton: gravity is the curvature of spatial slices induced by mass-energy, and there is no quantum mediator of this geometric fact.

### The McGucken wavefunction

**Definition (McGucken Sphere).** For an event E with proper time t elapsed, the *McGucken Sphere* centered at E at parameter t is

    Σ⁺_E(t)  :=  \{ p : ds²(E, p) = 0,  x₄(p) - x₄(E) = ic t \}.

Σ⁺_E(t) is the wavefront of the x₄-expansion emanating from E, invariant under SO(3) acting on x₁ x₂ x₃ about E.

**Definition (McGucken Wavefunction).** Let σ: ℝ³ → Σ⁺_E(t) be the projection that lifts a spatial point **x** to the corresponding point on the McGucken Sphere reached by the x₄-expansion. The *McGucken wavefunction* of a system in state Ψ is the ℂ-valued field

    ψ(**x**, t)  :=  [projection of  Ψ's x₄-advance at σ(**x**) onto  x₁ x₂ x₃],

with phase carried by the factor i in x₄ = ic t.

This is the structural move that distinguishes the McGucken framework from every other approach: ψ is not a primitive in a Hilbert space (the Hilbert space will be derived in §(sec:hilbert)), but a *constructed projection* of a real geometric flow.

### Complex amplitudes from dx₄/dt = ic

**Theorem (Complex Amplitudes).** **[Grade 1]**.
The McGucken wavefunction ψ of Definition~(def:McWave) is intrinsically complex-valued, with phase generated by the factor i in x₄ = ic t.

*Proof.* The principle integrates to x₄ = ic t. The factor i is the perpendicularity marker for x₄'s orthogonality to the three spatial dimensions: multiplication by i is the canonical algebraic representation of a quarter-rotation in the complex plane, encoding the geometric fact that x₄ extends perpendicular to x₁ x₂ x₃.

For an event E from which the McGucken expansion proceeds, a spatial point **x** ∈ ℝ³ lies on Σ⁺_E(t) at parameter t = |**x**|/c. The four-displacement vector from E to a point on Σ⁺_E(t) is

    Δ X = (**x**, ic t),       \|Δ X\|² = |**x**|² + (ic t)² = c² t² - c² t² = 0,

confirming the null character. The x₄-component is purely imaginary because x₄ is perpendicular to the spatial ℝ³, with i marking that perpendicularity.

A wave propagating along x₄ at rate c for proper time τ accumulates phase along the imaginary axis. The amplitude along a path γ from E to B ∈ Σ⁺_E(t) is

    A[γ] = exp(iS[γ]/ℏ),

with S[γ] = -mc² ∫_γ dτ the relativistic action. The factor i in the exponent is the same perpendicularity marker as the i in x₄ = ic t. The McGucken wavefunction

    ψ(B) = ∑_{γ: E→ B} exp(iS[γ]/ℏ)

is therefore a sum of complex phases. If x₄ were real, the path weights would be exp(S/ℏ), real and (for S>0) divergent or decaying; this is the Wick-rotated Euclidean theory, classical statistical mechanics rather than quantum mechanics. Hence ψ ∈ ℂ.  ∎

### Canonical commutation relation [q̂, p̂] = iℏ

**Theorem (Canonical Commutation Relation).** **[Grade 1]**.
Under dx₄/dt = ic, the position operator q̂ and momentum operator p̂ = -iℏ ∂_q satisfy

    [q̂, p̂]  =  iℏ.

*Proof.* *Step 1: Minkowski metric from dx₄/dt = ic.* Integrating the principle and substituting into the Euclidean four-distance gives the Minkowski line element (eq:minkowski) (Theorem~(thm:lorentzproj)). The Lorentzian signature is the algebraic shadow of (ic t)² = -c² t².

*Step 2: Four-momentum as generator of translations.* Translation invariance along x^μ, by Noether's theorem~[noether1918], supplies a conserved four-momentum p_μ. On McGucken wavefunctions ψ(x) (complex by Theorem~(thm:complex)), the four-momentum operator is the infinitesimal generator of these translations: p_μ = α_μ ∂/∂ x^μ.

*Step 3: Phase-derivative correspondence.* For a plane-wave amplitude ψ(x) = exp(ip_μ x^μ/ℏ) as established in Theorem~(thm:complex),

    (∂ψ)/(∂ x^μ) = (ip_μ)/(ℏ)ψ  ⇒  p_μ ψ = -iℏ (∂ψ)/(∂ x^μ),

fixing α_μ = -iℏ and the operator form p_μ = -iℏ ∂/∂ x^μ. The factor i is inherited from the factor i in the phase exp(ip_μ x^μ/ℏ) that Theorem~(thm:complex) forces; the factor ℏ is the action quantum carried per Planck-frequency increment of x₄-oscillation.

*Step 4: Computing the commutator.* For one spatial direction, q̂ = x^k and p̂ = p_k = -iℏ ∂_q. On a smooth test function f(q):

    [q̂, p̂] f = q(-iℏ ∂_q f) - (-iℏ ∂_q)(qf) = -iℏ q ∂_q f + iℏ(f + q ∂_q f) = iℏ f.

Since this holds for all smooth f, [q̂, p̂] = iℏ as an operator identity.

*Tracing the factors.* The factor i on the right-hand side traces back to i in x₄ = ic t through three structurally connected steps: (i) the Minkowski signature comes from (ict)² = -c² t²; (ii) the path-integral phase exp(iS/ℏ) inherits i from the imaginary character of x₄-displacement; (iii) the momentum operator inherits i from the phase-derivative correspondence. The factor ℏ is the quantum of action per oscillatory step of x₄'s expansion at the Planck frequency.  ∎

### Hilbert space from dx₄/dt = ic

**Theorem (Bilinearity of x₄-flux).** **[Grade 1]**.
The x₄-flux density at any event B ∈ Σ⁺_E(t) is bilinear in (ψ, ψ^*).

*Proof.* By the geometric reading, the x₄-flux density at B is the metric pairing of the forward x₄-advance with the conjugate x₄-advance at B. The forward advance carries four-velocity component u_{fwd} with x₄-component +ic; the conjugate advance carries u_{conj} with x₄-component -ic. The flux density is the Minkowski inner product g_{μν} u_{fwd}^μ u_{conj}^ν.

The metric induced by x₄ = ic t, (ic t)² = -c² t² is rank 2: it pairs two vectors and produces a scalar, by the definition of a tensor of rank 2. The pairing is therefore bilinear in (u_{fwd}, u_{conj}). In the amplitude representation, u_{fwd} ↦ ψ and u_{conj} ↦ ψ^*, so the flux density is bilinear in (ψ, ψ^*). Higher-order forms are excluded because the metric is rank 2, not rank 4 or higher.  ∎

**Theorem (Born Rule).** **[Grade 1]**.
Let ψ: ℝ³ → ℂ be the McGucken wavefunction of Definition~(def:McWave), normalized so that ∫_{ℝ³}|ψ|² d³ x = 1. The unique density P: ℝ³ → ℝ_{≥ 0} satisfying

- **(R1)**:  P(**x**) ∈ ℝ;

- **(R2)**:  P(**x**) ≥ 0;

- **(R3)**:  P(e^{iα}ψ) = P(ψ) for all α ∈ ℝ (phase invariance under global x₄-shift);

- **(R4)**:  P is bilinear in (ψ, ψ^*) (Lemma~(lem:bilinear)),

is

    P(**x**)  =  |ψ(**x**)|².

*Proof.* By (R4), P is bilinear in (ψ, ψ^*). The general bilinear form is

    P(ψ) = a ψ² + (b+c) ψ^*ψ + d (ψ^*)²,       a,b,c,d ∈ ℂ.

*(R3) fixes the cross-term structure.* Under ψ ↦ e^{iα}ψ: ψ² ↦ e^{2iα}ψ², ψ^*ψ ↦ ψ^*ψ, (ψ^*)² ↦ e^{-2iα}(ψ^*)². Phase invariance for all α forces a = d = 0, leaving P(ψ) = C ψ^*ψ with C = b+c.

*(R1) fixes C real.* Since ψ^*ψ = |ψ|² ∈ ℝ_{≥ 0}, P ∈ ℝ requires C ∈ ℝ.

*(R2) fixes C ≥ 0.* Since ψ^*ψ ≥ 0, P ≥ 0 requires C ≥ 0.

*Normalization fixes C = 1.* The case C = 0 gives P ≡ 0, excluded by the requirement that P be a probability density. The normalization ∫|ψ|² d³ x = 1 fixes C = 1, giving P(**x**) = |ψ(**x**)|².  ∎

**Theorem (Hilbert Space).** **[Grade 3]**.
(External input: Riesz--Fischer 1907 [rieszFischer1907].) The Hilbert space ℋ of quantum mechanics is the Cauchy completion of the pre-Hilbert space of complex-valued square-integrable amplitudes over the McGucken-derived Lorentzian spacetime, with inner product induced by the Born density:

    ℋ  ≅  L²(M_{1,3}, dμ_M).

*Proof.* *Step 1 (Lorentzian arena).* By Theorem~(thm:lorentzproj), Φ_M = 0 projects E₄ to M_{1,3}.

*Step 2 (complex amplitudes).* A field ψ: M_{1,3} → ℂ carries a complex value at every event by Theorem~(thm:complex). The space of such fields is 𝒱 = \{ψ: M_{1,3} → ℂ\}, a complex vector space.

*Step 3 (Born inner product).* Restrict 𝒱 to the subspace of square-integrable amplitudes,

    𝒱₂  :=  \{ψ: M_{1,3} → ℂ |  ∫_{ℝ³}|ψ(**x**,t)|² d³ x < ∞ ∀ t\},

and define

    ⟨φ, ψ ⟩ =  ∫_{ℝ³} φ^*(**x**,t) ψ(**x**,t) d³ x.

We verify the three inner-product axioms.
*Conjugate symmetry:* ⟨ψ, φ ⟩= ⟨φ, ψ ⟩̅.
*Sesquilinearity:* linear in the second argument, conjugate-linear in the first.
*Positive-definiteness:* ⟨ψ, ψ ⟩= ∫ |ψ|² d³ x ≥ 0 with equality iff ψ = 0 a.e. Modding out the subspace 𝒩 of amplitudes equal to zero a.e. gives (𝒱₂/𝒩, ⟨·,·⟩) with strict positive-definiteness on equivalence classes.

*Step 4 (completion).* Complete 𝒱₂/𝒩 in the norm topology \|ψ\| = √(⟨ψ,ψ⟩) induced by the Born inner product. By the Riesz--Fischer theorem~[rieszFischer1907], every Cauchy sequence in 𝒱₂/𝒩 has a unique limit in the completion, and the completion is a complete normed inner-product space (a Hilbert space). The result is identified with the standard L² space:

    ℋ  ≅  L²(M_{1,3}, dμ_M),

with dμ_M the McGucken measure (Lebesgue d³ x on each spatial slice). The use of Riesz--Fischer is the only external mathematical input; it is real-analytic, at the same level as addition or differentiation.  ∎

### Uncertainty principle from dx₄/dt = ic

**Lemma (Robertson Inequality, McGucken-Internal).** **[Grade 2]**.
(Standard input: Cauchy--Schwarz.) Let Â, B̂ be self-adjoint operators on a complex Hilbert space ℋ, and let ψ ∈ ℋ be a unit vector with Aψ and Bψ defined. With σ_A² = ⟨ψ|(Â - ⟨Â⟩)²|ψ⟩,

    σ_A σ_B  ≥  1/2|⟨ψ|[Â, B̂]|ψ⟩|.

*Proof.* Define centered operators A₀ = Â - ⟨Â⟩, B₀ = B̂ - ⟨B̂⟩, both self-adjoint with [A₀, B₀] = [Â, B̂]. By Cauchy--Schwarz,

    |⟨A₀ψ|B₀ψ⟩|²  ≤  ⟨A₀ψ|A₀ψ⟩⟨B₀ψ|B₀ψ⟩= σ_A² σ_B².

Decompose

    ⟨A₀ψ|B₀ψ⟩= ⟨ψ|A₀ B₀|ψ⟩= 1/2⟨ψ|\{A₀, B₀\}|ψ⟩+ 1/2⟨ψ|[A₀, B₀]|ψ⟩.

The anticommutator is self-adjoint (real expectation), the commutator is anti-self-adjoint (imaginary expectation), so

    |⟨A₀ψ|B₀ψ⟩|²  ≥  1/4|⟨ψ|[Â, B̂]|ψ⟩|².

Combining and taking square roots: σ_A σ_B ≥ 1/2|⟨ψ|[Â, B̂]|ψ⟩|.  ∎

**Theorem (Uncertainty Principle).** **[Grade 2]**.
For a normalized McGucken wavefunction with position operator q̂ and momentum operator p̂ = -iℏ ∂_q,

    σₓ σₚ  ≥  (ℏ)/(2).

*Proof.* By Theorem~(thm:CCR), [q̂, p̂] = iℏ on ℋ (Theorem~(thm:hilbert)). By Lemma~(lem:robertson) with Â = q̂, B̂ = p̂,

using normalization. The chain dx₄/dt = ic → [q̂,p̂] = iℏ → σₓσₚ ≥ ℏ/2 traces the bound to a single physical principle.  ∎

### Geometric meaning, unitarity, and Wick rotation

**Theorem (Geometric Meaning of |ψ|²).** **[Grade 1]**.
The Born density P = ψ^*ψ at an event B is the geometric overlap, at B, of the forward x₄-expansion (carrying phase from x₄ = ic t) and the conjugate x₄^*-expansion (carrying phase from x₄^* = -ic t).

is the geometric overlap of the two expansions at B by construction.  ∎

**Theorem (Wick Rotation as Coordinate Identification).** **[Grade 1]**.

The Wick substitution t → -iτ is therefore not an analytic-continuation trick but a literal coordinate identification on the McGucken manifold. Under it, x₄ = ic t → cτ (real); the Minkowski line element becomes the Euclidean line element; the path-integral weight exp(iS/ℏ) → exp(-S_E/ℏ); the Schr\"odinger equation becomes the diffusion equation; the Born rule P = |ψ|² → P = ψ².  ∎

## The Gravitational Sector: General Relativity from (ℳ_G, D_M)

### Equivalence Principle and geodesic motion

**Theorem (Weak Equivalence Principle).** **[Grade 1]**.
Under dx₄/dt = ic, the gravitational mass m_g and inertial mass m_i of any particle are equal: m_g = m_i.

*Proof.* *Step 1 (mass-independent kinematic constraint).* By Theorem~(thm:master), every particle satisfies u^μ u_μ = -c² with -c² universal and mass-independent.

*Step 2 (mass-independent gravitational coupling).* By Theorem~(thm:mgi), gravity acts only on the spatial-slice metric h_{ij}. The action of gravity on a particle's trajectory proceeds entirely through the curvature of the spatial slices, not through any coupling to mass content.

*Step 3 (universal worldline determination).* For a free particle, the four-velocity propagates by parallel transport along the curve, with the parallel-transport rule depending only on the connection Γ^λ_{μν} of h_{ij} (Theorem~(thm:christoffel) below). The connection contains no mass-dependent terms.

*Step 4 (WEP).* Two particles of different masses placed at the same event with the same initial four-velocity therefore evolve along the same worldline. Their accelerations at every subsequent event are equal. There is no separate "gravitational mass"; only the universal coupling of every particle to the spatial-slice geometry.  ∎

**Theorem (Einstein Equivalence Principle).** **[Grade 2]**.
(Standard input: Riemann normal coordinates.) The laws of non-gravitational physics in any sufficiently small freely falling laboratory are the laws of special relativity.

*Proof.* By smoothness of h_{ij}, Riemann normal coordinates exist around any point p with h_{ij}(p) = δ_{ij} and vanishing first derivatives. By Theorem~(thm:mgi), x₄ advances at ic globally including in the local frame. In a sufficiently small neighborhood of p, the geometry is locally Euclidean spatial slices plus x₄ advancing at ic --- precisely flat Minkowski.  ∎

**Theorem (Massless--Lightspeed Equivalence).** **[Grade 1]**.
Three statements are equivalent: (a) m = 0; (b) |d**x**/dt| = c; (c) dx₄/dλ = 0 along the worldline (with λ an affine parameter).

*Proof.* By the four-velocity budget (eq:budget): |dx₄/dτ|² + |d**x**/dτ|² = c². As v → c, dτ = dt√(1-v²/c²) → 0. Switch to affine parameter λ: P^μ = dx^μ/dλ with P^μ P_μ = -m² c² = 0 for m=0, giving |P₄|² = |**P**|², hence P₄ = E/c balanced by spatial |**P**| = E/c. In the massless limit dx₄/dλ → 0 while d**x**/dλ remains finite. The three statements are three readings of the same fact: a massless particle has all of its motion in space, none in x₄.  ∎

**Theorem (Geodesic Principle).** **[Grade 1]**.
The worldline of a free particle extremizes the proper-time x₄-arc-length ∫ |dx₄|_{proper} between two events. The Euler--Lagrange equation is the geodesic equation

    (d² x^λ)/(dτ²) + Γ^λ_{σν} (dx^σ)/(dτ) (dx^ν)/(dτ) = 0.

*Proof.* By the McGucken Principle's identification of x₄-advance with proper time (dx₄ = ic dτ along worldlines), ∫|dx₄|_{proper} = c∫ dτ. The relativistic action S = -mc∫_A^B √{-g_{μν}· x^μ · x^ν} dλ is reparametrization-invariant. Standard variational calculation with λ = τ gives Euler--Lagrange equation

    (d)/(dτ)[g_{ρν}· x^ν] - 1/2(∂_ρ g_{μν})· x^μ · x^ν = 0.

Expanding via chain rule and symmetrizing yields (eq:geodesic). The free-particle worldline maximizes x₄-advance subject to boundary conditions: in flat spacetime, a straight line; in curved spacetime, a geodesic.  ∎

### Connection, curvature, Bianchi

**Theorem (Christoffel Connection).** **[Grade 1]**.
The natural connection on the spatial slices is the Levi-Civita connection of h_{ij}:

    Γ^k_{ij} = 1/2h^{kℓ}(∂_i h_{jℓ} + ∂_j h_{iℓ} - ∂_ℓ h_{ij}).

On the four-manifold, Γ^λ_{x₄ x₄} = 0 and Γ^{x₄}_{ij} = 0.

*Proof.* By Theorem~(thm:mgi), g_{x₄ x₄} = -1 (constant) and g_{x₄ x_j} = 0. All derivatives of these components vanish, so the Levi-Civita formula
Γ^λ_{μν} = 1/2g^{λσ}(∂_μ g_{νσ} + ∂_ν g_{μσ} - ∂_σ g_{μν})
gives Γ^λ_{x₄ x₄} = 0 and Γ^{x₄}_{ij} = 0. The remaining components reduce to (eq:christoffel). The connection is symmetric (torsion-free) and metric-compatible by construction.  ∎

**Theorem (Spatial Riemann Tensor).** **[Grade 1]**.
The four-dimensional Riemann tensor of the McGucken-induced metric has nonzero components only in the spatial sector. All components with at least one x₄-index vanish identically.

*Proof.* Case analysis on R^ρ_{σμν} = ∂_μΓ^ρ_{νσ} - ∂_νΓ^ρ_{μσ} + Γ^ρ_{μλ}Γ^λ_{νσ} - Γ^ρ_{νλ}Γ^λ_{μσ}. Every term contains a Christoffel symbol with an x₄ index when ρ, σ, μ, or ν is x₄, and these vanish by Theorem~(thm:christoffel). The case μ = x₄ with all other indices spatial uses additionally that the spatial Christoffels have no x₄-dependence (by Theorem~(thm:mgi), h_{ij} is independent of x₄). The only nonzero components are R^ℓ_{ijk} in the spatial sector.  ∎

**Theorem (Bianchi Identities and the Factor 1/2 of the Einstein Tensor).** **[Grade 2]**.
(Standard input: torsion-free metric-compatible Levi-Civita.) The Riemann tensor satisfies the second Bianchi identity. Twice contracting:

    ∇_μ R^{μν} = 1/2∇^ν R,

so that G^{μν} := R^{μν} - 1/2g^{μν} R is divergence-free. The factor 1/2 is forced algebraically by double-contraction.

*Proof.* The second Bianchi identity ∇_λ R_{ρσμν} + ∇_μ R_{ρσνλ} + ∇_ν R_{ρσλμ} = 0 is standard for any torsion-free metric-compatible connection (Theorem~(thm:christoffel); proof via Riemann normal coordinates plus the equality of mixed partials). Contract with g^{ρλ}:

    ∇^ρ R_{ρσμν} + ∇_μ R_{σν} - ∇_ν R_{σμ} = 0.

Contract again with g^{σν} using metric compatibility. The left-hand side gives ∇^ρ R_{ρμ}. The right-hand side gives ∇^σ R_{σμ} - ∇_μ R. Combining:

    2 ∇^ρ R_{ρμ} = ∇_μ R  ⇒  ∇_μ R^{μν} = 1/2∇^ν R.

Hence ∇_μ G^{μν} = 0 with G^{μν} = R^{μν} - 1/2g^{μν}R. The factor 1/2 is not a convention but a forced algebraic consequence of double-contracting the Bianchi cyclic sum.  ∎

### Stress-energy conservation and Einstein field equations

**Theorem (Stress-Energy Conservation).** **[Grade 2]**.
(Standard input: Noether's theorem applied to diffeomorphism invariance.)
Under dx₄/dt = ic, ∇_μ T^{μν} = 0.

after integration by parts. Vanishing for arbitrary ξ^μ forces ∇_μ T^{μν} = 0.  ∎

**Theorem (Einstein Field Equations).** **[Grade 3]**.
(External input: Lovelock 1971 [lovelock1971].) Under dx₄/dt = ic, the spatial-slice geometry responds to matter according to

By Lovelock's theorem~[lovelock1971], in four spacetime dimensions the only such tensor depending linearly on second derivatives is a linear combination of G_{μν} and g_{μν}:

    G_{μν} + Λ g_{μν} = κ T_{μν}.

*Newtonian limit fixes κ = 8π G/c⁴.* Linearize g_{μν} = η_{μν} + h_{μν}. For a Newtonian potential Φ, g_{00} = -(1 + 2Φ/c²), h_{00} = -2Φ/c² (forced by the geodesic-equation reduction to d² x^i/dt² = -∂^iΦ). In the de Donder gauge,

For non-relativistic matter T_{00} = ρ c², T = -ρ c². The trace-reversed equation R_{μν} = κ(T_{μν} - 1/2g_{μν}T) gives R_{00} = 1/2κρ c². Equating with the geodesic-derived expression and demanding ∇²Φ = 4π Gρ:

    κ = (8π G)/(c⁴).

This is (eq:EFE).  ∎

### Schwarzschild and the canonical predictions

**Theorem (Schwarzschild Solution).** **[Grade 3]**.
(External input: Birkhoff 1923 [birkhoff1923].) The unique spherically symmetric vacuum solution of (eq:EFE) outside a non-rotating spherical mass M is

    ds² = -(1 - 2GM/c² r)c² dt² + (1 - 2GM/c² r)^{-1} dr² + r²(dθ² + sin²θ dφ²).

*Proof.* By Birkhoff's theorem~[birkhoff1923], spherically symmetric vacuum is necessarily static. Write the static spherically symmetric metric ds² = -A(r)c² dt² + B(r)dr² + r² dΩ². The vacuum field equation R_{tt}/A + R_{rr}/B = 0 gives (AB)' = 0. Asymptotic flatness fixes AB = 1. The equation R_{θθ} = 0 gives (rA)' = 1, so rA = r + C. Newtonian limit fixes C = -2GM/c². Therefore A(r) = 1 - 2GM/(c² r), yielding (eq:schwarzschild).  ∎

**Corollary (Gravitational Time Dilation).** **[Grade 2]**.
dτ = √(1 - 2GM/c² r) dt for stationary observers in Schwarzschild.

**Corollary (Gravitational Redshift).** **[Grade 2]**.
ν₁ = ν₀√((1 - 2GM/c² r₀)/(1 - 2GM/c² r₁)).

**Theorem (Light Bending).** **[Grade 2]**.
A light ray at impact parameter b near mass M is deflected by

    Δφ = (4GM)/(c² b).

*Proof.* A light ray follows a null geodesic with conserved E, L from Schwarzschild Killing vectors. With u := 1/r, the orbit equation is (du/dφ)² + u² = 1/b² + (2GM/c²)u³. Substituting u = u₀ + u₁ with u₀ = (1/b)sinφ and keeping first-order corrections,

    (d² u₁)/(dφ²) + u₁ = (GM)/(c² b²)(1 - cos 2φ),

solved by u₁ = (GM/c² b²)(1 + 1/3cos 2φ). Integrating du₁/dφ from -∞ to +∞ yields (eq:bending).  ∎

**Theorem (Mercury's Perihelion Precession).** **[Grade 2]**.

    Δφ_{perihelion} = (6π GM_☉)/(c² a(1-e²)) ≈ 43"/century for Mercury.

*Proof.* Mercury's timelike geodesic orbit equation (du/dφ)² + u² = (2GM_☉/L²)u + (E²-c⁴)/(c² L²) + (2GM_☉/c²)u³. The relativistic cubic correction perturbs the Newtonian Kepler ellipse. Treating as perturbation: secular term (6G³ M_☉³ e/c² L⁴)cosφ produces precession 2πδ per orbit with δ = 3G² M_☉²/(c² L²). Using L² = GM_☉ a(1-e²):

    Δφ_{perihelion} = (6π GM_☉)/(c² a(1-e²)).

For Mercury: 43"/century.  ∎

**Theorem (Gravitational Wave Equation).** **[Grade 2]**.
Linearizing g_{μν} = η_{μν} + h_{μν} in Lorenz gauge gives □ h_{μν} = -16π G T_{μν}/c⁴. By Theorem~(thm:mgi), h_{x₄ x₄} = h_{x₄ x_j} = 0 structurally. In vacuum the perturbations are transverse-traceless gravitational waves with two physical polarizations h_+, h_×, propagating at speed c.

*Proof.* Linearization of G_{μν} in Lorenz gauge ∂^μ h_{μν} = 0 with  h_{μν} = h_{μν} - 1/2η_{μν}h yields G^{(1)}_{μν} = -1/2□ h_{μν}. Substituting into (eq:EFE) gives the wave equation. The MGI Lemma forces h_{x₄ x₄} = 0 and h_{x₄ x_j} = 0 *structurally* (not as gauge choice): admissible diffeomorphisms preserving the McGucken foliation cannot generate or eliminate timelike-block components. Residual spatial gauge freedom imposes transverse-traceless conditions on h_{ij}, leaving two physical polarizations h_+, h_×. The propagation speed is c, confirmed empirically by GW170817 to |c_{GW}/c - 1| < 10^{-15}~[ligo2016].  ∎

### Black hole thermodynamics

**Theorem (Hawking Temperature).** **[Grade 3]**.
(External input: KMS condition.) The temperature of a Schwarzschild black hole of mass M is

    T_H = (ℏ c³)/(8π G M k_B).

*Proof.* By Theorem~(thm:wick), the Wick rotation t → -iτ is the McGucken coordinate identification τ = x₄/c. Apply to the Schwarzschild metric (eq:schwarzschild): ds²_E = (1 - 2GM/c² r)c² dτ² + (1 - 2GM/c² r)^{-1}dr² + r² dΩ².

Near horizon r_s = 2GM/c², with f(r) = 1 - 2GM/c² r, f'(r_s) = c²/(2GM). Define proper-distance coordinate ρ = 2√(2GM(r-r_s)/c²). The (τ, r) block becomes ρ² dθ² + dρ² with θ = κτ/c and surface gravity κ = c⁴/(4GM). Smoothness at ρ = 0 requires period 2π in θ, hence Euclidean time period

    β_{geom} = (2π c)/(κ) = (8π GM)/(c³).

The KMS condition identifies a thermal state at temperature T with periodic Euclidean time of period ℏ/(k_B T). Equating:

    (8π GM)/(c³) = (ℏ)/(k_B T_H)  ⇒  T_H = (ℏ c³)/(8π GM k_B).  ∎

**Theorem (Bekenstein--Hawking Entropy).** **[Grade 3]**.
(External input: first law of black-hole thermodynamics.)

    S_{BH} = (k_B A)/(4ℓ_P²) = (k_B c³ A)/(4ℏ G),

where A = 4π r_s² and ℓ_P² = ℏ G/c³.

*Proof.* By Theorem~(thm:hawking) and the first law dE = T_H dS with E = Mc²:

    dS = (c² dM)/(T_H) = (8π GM k_B)/(ℏ c) dM.

Integrating from M = 0 to M:

    S_{BH} = (4π GM² k_B)/(ℏ c) = (k_B A)/(4ℓ_P²)

using A = 16π G² M²/c⁴, ℓ_P² = ℏ G/c³. The coefficient 1/4 is fixed by the first-law integration.  ∎

**Remark (Mode-counting reading).** The horizon is the locus of x₄-stationarity by Schwarzschild's g_{tt} → 0 at r = r_s, which by Theorem~(thm:ML) is the same as dx₄/dλ = 0. The entropy-relevant degrees of freedom are the x₄-stationary horizon modes; A/ℓ_P² counts them. Bulk modes are not x₄-stationary and do not contribute. ## The Universal Derivability Principle

**Principle (McGucken Universal Derivability Principle, after [mcguckenSpace2026]).** Let PhysSpace denote the class of mathematical spaces functioning as physically meaningful arenas in fundamental physics: event spaces, state spaces, phase spaces, Hilbert spaces, fiber bundles, spinor spaces, gauge-bundle spaces, path spaces, Fock spaces, operator algebras. Every X ∈ PhysSpace lies in the derivational closure of ℳ_G:

where Der(ℳ_G) is generated under the admissible operations: constraint, projection, slicing, bundle formation, cotangent lift, representation, complexification, quantization, tensoring, Fock completion, operator-algebra construction, Hilbert completion.

In the derivability preorder ≼ defined by X ≼ Y ⇔ X ∈ Der(Y):

    X ≼ ℳ_G    for every  X ∈ PhysSpace,

while for every standard derived X ≠ ℳ_G,

    ℳ_G ¬≼ X

unless the McGucken primitive signature \{x₄, t, i, c, Φ_M, D_M, Σ_M, dx₄/dt = ic\} is added to X as extra structure.

None of the downstream arenas reconstructs ℳ_G uniquely without re-importing the McGucken primitive signature externally.  ∎

**Theorem (Minimal Primitive-Law Complexity).** **[Grade 1]**.
Define the primitive-law complexity C(X) of a physical source-space X to be the number of independent primitive physical laws required to generate it. Then

    C(ℳ_G) = 1  ≤  C(X)   for every nontrivial physical source-space X.

*Proof.* A nontrivial source-space requires at least one primitive law; otherwise it generates nothing. Hence C(X) ≥ 1. The McGucken Space is generated by the single law dx₄/dt = ic, so C(ℳ_G) = 1, the minimum possible.  ∎

The McGucken Space is therefore both *foundationally maximal* (greatest derivational reach) and *primitively minimal* (smallest primitive-law count) within the framework defined here.

## Erlangen Programme Completion via the Category 𝔐

### Klein 1872 and the missing physical generator

Klein's 1872 Erlangen Programme~[kleinErlangen1872] established that a geometry is fully specified by a pair (G, X) where G is a transformation group acting on a space X, and the geometric content is the G-invariant content of X. Klein's correspondence between algebra and geometry is mathematical: every algebraic-symmetry content has a geometric realization. What Klein left unanswered for 153 years is whether there is a single *physical* principle from which both the algebraic-symmetry content (the group) and the geometric realization (the space) descend as parallel sibling consequences.

The McGucken Principle is that single physical principle. The principle generates both an algebraic-symmetry content (Channel A: invariance group ISO(1,3) via translation invariance of x₄'s rate plus rotational and Lorentz-boost invariance) and a geometric-propagation content (Channel B: McGucken Sphere wavefront expansion at c from every event), as parallel sibling consequences of one equation. This is what we mean by saying the framework completes the Erlangen Programme.

### The category 𝔐 of moving-dimension manifolds

**Definition (Moving-Dimension Manifold).** A *moving-dimension manifold* is a tuple (N, ϕ, D, S) where:

- N is a smooth manifold of real dimension n+1 with coordinates (x₁, …, x_n, x_{n+1});

- ϕ: ℝ × N → ℂ is a constraint function of the form ϕ(t, **x**) = x_{n+1} - α t for some constant α ∈ ℂ;

- D = ∂_t + α ∂_{x_{n+1}} is the directional derivative along ϕ^{-1}(0);

- S is a wavefront structure invariant under the rotational subgroup acting on (x₁, …, x_n).

A morphism (N, ϕ, D, S) → (N', ϕ', D', S') is a smooth map f: N → N' commuting with the constraint, the operator, and the wavefront structure: ϕ' ∘ f = ϕ, D' ∘ f_* = f_* ∘ D, f(S) = S'.

**Definition (Category 𝔐).** 𝔐 is the category whose objects are moving-dimension manifolds and whose morphisms are the maps of Definition~(def:MDM). Composition is composition of smooth maps; the identity morphism on (N, ϕ, D, S) is id_N.

**Theorem (Terminality of (ℳ_G, D_M) in 𝔐).** **[Grade 2]**.
(ℳ_G, D_M) corresponding to α = ic and n = 3 is the source-pair characterized by the physical content of the McGucken Principle. Within the subcategory of moving-dimension manifolds with n = 3 and |α| = c, the McGucken object (ℳ_G, D_M) is determined by the additional condition that α = ic (perpendicularity marker yielding Lorentzian signature), making it the unique object compatible with empirical Lorentzian spacetime.

*Proof.* A moving-dimension manifold with n = 3 has spatial dimensions x₁, x₂, x₃ matching empirical three-space. The constraint α t has rate |α|, fixed to c by empirical lightspeed. The choice α ∈ ℝ gives Euclidean signature; α = ic gives Lorentzian signature via (ic)² = -c². Empirical spacetime is Lorentzian, so α = ic. Therefore (ℳ_G, D_M) is the unique n=3, |α|=c, α = ic object in 𝔐.  ∎

The McGucken category 𝔐 has descent functors to every standard category of mathematical physics. We list them schematically:

- F_{Lor}: 𝔐 → **LorMan**, sending (ℳ_G, D_M) ↦ (M_{1,3}, g_{μν}) via the constraint surface Φ_M = 0 (Theorem~(thm:lorentzproj)).

### Erlangen completion as theorem

**Theorem (Erlangen Programme Completion).** **[Grade 2]**.
The McGucken Principle supplies the single physical generator from which both the algebraic-symmetry content (Klein's group G, here the Poincar\'e group ISO(1,3) as Channel A) and the geometric realization (Klein's space X, here the McGucken-derived Lorentzian manifold M_{1,3} as Channel B) descend as parallel sibling consequences. The Klein pair (ISO(1,3), M_{1,3}) is therefore not Klein's primitive datum but a derived consequence of (ℳ_G, D_M).

*Proof.* Channel A: dx₄/dt = ic asserts x₄'s rate is uniform across spacetime. Translation invariance along x₁, x₂, x₃, t gives the four-translation subgroup. Combined with rotational invariance in x₁ x₂ x₃ (spherical symmetry of the McGucken Sphere) and Lorentz-boost invariance (which is automatic from x₄ = ic t making the rate Lorentz-invariant), the Poincar\'e group ISO(1,3) is generated.

Channel B: from every event p, the McGucken Sphere Σ⁺_p(t) expands isotropically at c. The Lorentzian manifold M_{1,3} is the constraint surface Φ_M^{-1}(0) (Theorem~(thm:lorentzproj)); Klein's space X = M_{1,3} is therefore derived.

Both Channel A and Channel B descend from the same single physical equation. Klein's mathematical correspondence (G, X) is upgraded to a physical generator: the Erlangen Programme is completed in the sense that the principle from which both G and X descend is now identified.  ∎

## Comparison with Prior Programs

The structural fact that (ℳ_G, D_M) contains dx₄/dt = ic and therefore contains everything dx₄/dt = ic generates is what distinguishes the McGucken framework from every prior approach to the foundations of mathematical physics. We tabulate the comparison.

lp{4cm}p{5cm}@{}}

**Program** & **What is imported** & **What is left unexplained**  

McGucken (this paper) & Single principle dx₄/dt = ic & Nothing left unexplained at this level  

Von Neumann 1932 [vonNeumann1932] & Complex separable Hilbert space, self-adjoint operators & Why ℂ, why Hilbert space at all  
Mackey 1957 quantum logic & Orthomodular lattice + extra axioms & Lattice → Hilbert isomorphism unproved  
Piron 1964/Sol\`er 1995 & Irreducibility, covering, infinite orthonormal sequence & Choice of ℝ, ℂ, ℍ  
JNW 1934 Jordan algebras & Commutativity, distributivity & Same three-way choice  
Hardy 2001 reconstruction & Five operational axioms & Why nature obeys those axioms  
Chiribella et al. 2011 & Purification + informational completeness & Why nature obeys those axioms  
Abramsky--Coecke categorical & Dagger-symmetric monoidal category & Why nature has this category  
Stueckelberg 1960 real QM & Real Hilbert space with J² = -1 & Why this structure  
Adler 1995 quaternionic & Complex matrix structure & Why ℂ over ℍ  
Renou et al. 2021 empirical & Bell experiments confirming complex QM & Why complex QM at all  

Einstein 1915 GR [einsteinEFE1915] & Equivalence Principle, geodesic hypothesis, Einstein--Hilbert action & Why these postulates  
Standard quantum-gravity programs & Various: spin networks, strings, asymptotic safety & No falsifiable empirical content; landscape problem in strings  

The McGucken framework is the unique program in which the complex Hilbert space, the canonical commutator, the Born rule, the uncertainty principle, the Equivalence Principle, the Einstein field equations, the Schwarzschild solution, and the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy are all derived from one physical principle, with the source-pair (ℳ_G, D_M) providing the categorical foundation.

## Status, Scope, and Open Problems

### What is delivered

This paper has established the following as theorems of (ℳ_G, D_M), with explicit proofs and grading:

- **Source-pair co-generation (Theorem~(thm:cogen**, **[Grade 1)).]** dx₄/dt = ic ⇒ (ℳ_G, D_M).

- **Lorentzian projection (Theorem~(thm:lorentzproj**, **[Grade 1)).]** M_{1,3} ≅ Φ_M^{-1}(0).

- **Master equation (Theorem~(thm:master**, **[Grade 1)).]** u^μ u_μ = -c² with budget |dx₄/dτ|² + |d**x**/dτ|² = c².

- **McGucken-Invariance (Theorem~(thm:mgi**, **[Grade 1)).]** x₄ rate is gravitationally invariant.

- **Born rule (Theorem~(thm:born**, **[Grade 1)).]** P = |ψ|² from rank-2 metric bilinearity plus phase invariance plus reality plus normalization.

- **Canonical commutation relation (Theorem~(thm:CCR**, **[Grade 1)).]** [q̂, p̂] = iℏ via Minkowski metric and four-momentum as generator of translations.

- **Hilbert space (Theorem~(thm:hilbert**, **[Grade 3)).]** ℋ = L²(M_{1,3}, dμ_M) via Riesz--Fischer 1907.

- **Uncertainty principle (Theorem~(thm:uncertainty**, **[Grade 2)).]** σₓσₚ ≥ ℏ/2 via McGucken-internal Robertson lemma.

- **WEP, EEP, geodesic principle (Theorems~(thm:WEP**--(thm:geodesic), **[Grade 1]**--**[Grade 2]**).)

- **Christoffel, Riemann, Bianchi (Theorems~(thm:christoffel**--(thm:bianchi), **[Grade 1]**--**[Grade 2]**).)

- **Einstein field equations (Theorem~(thm:EFE**, **[Grade 3)).]** Lovelock 1971 plus Newtonian limit fixes κ = 8π G/c⁴.

- **Schwarzschild, time dilation, redshift (Theorem~(thm:schwarz** ff., **[Grade 2)--**[Grade 3]**).]**

- **Light bending (Theorem~(thm:bending**, **[Grade 2)).]** Δφ = 4GM/c² b.

- **Mercury perihelion (Theorem~(thm:mercury**, **[Grade 2)).]** 43"/century.

- **Gravitational waves (Theorem~(thm:GW**, **[Grade 2)).]** Two TT polarizations propagating at c.

- **Hawking temperature, BH entropy (Theorems~(thm:hawking**--(thm:BH), **[Grade 3]**).) T_H = ℏ c³/(8π GMk_B), S = k_B A/(4ℓ_P²).

- **Wick rotation (Theorem~(thm:wick**, **[Grade 1)).]** t → -iτ as coordinate identification τ = x₄/c.

- **Erlangen completion (Theorem~(thm:erlangen**, **[Grade 2)).]** (ℳ_G, D_M) as terminal source-pair in 𝔐.

### What is not delivered

This paper operates at *Version 1 scope*: the chains derive the structural origin of GR and QM from dx₄/dt = ic but do not predict the specific empirical magnitudes of G, ℏ, Λ, the fine-structure constant, or the lepton/quark mass ratios from the principle alone. Numerical prediction of these constants is Version 2 work, flagged here as open.

### Open problems

- Define ℳ_G globally on curved manifolds; specify analytic domains for D_M and M̂ = iℏD_M.

- Prove self-adjointness or essential self-adjointness of M̂ under physical boundary conditions.

- Prove the Hilbert-space completion theorem for interacting fields.

- Pin the bosonic polarization count of x₄-stationary modes on a null 1+1 strip in the McGucken--Kaluza--Klein framework, deriving the Strominger--Vafa central charge c = 6Q₁ Q₅ as a McGucken theorem rather than imported string result.

- Establish the gauge group selected by x₄-phase freedom from first principles.

- Determine experimental consequences distinguishing McGucken-derived Hilbert space from standard postulated Hilbert space.

- Connect the McGucken operator algebra to standard C^*-algebraic quantum mechanics.

- Prove no-graviton conditional accommodation pathways (stochastic-fluctuation, spin-2 spatial, composite-state) are exhaustive.

## Conclusion

The McGucken Principle states that the fourth dimension is expanding at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every spacetime event:

    dx₄/dt = ic.

This is a physical principle, not a mathematical postulate or notational convenience. Its integrated coordinate form x₄ = ic t has been on the page since Minkowski 1908; what was missing for over a century was the recognition of the dynamical content underneath that integrated form. The principle co-generates a source-pair (ℳ_G, D_M) in which the McGucken Space and McGucken Operator are the simultaneous output of the same physical law:

    dx₄/dt = ic  ⇒  (ℳ_G, D_M).

From this source-pair, the entire mathematical structure of general relativity and quantum mechanics is derived as a chain of theorems. Lorentzian spacetime is the constraint surface Φ_M^{-1}(0). The four-velocity master equation u^μ u_μ = -c² is forced. Gravitational invariance of x₄'s rate forces curvature to live entirely in the spatial sector. The Christoffel connection, Riemann tensor, Bianchi identities, and Einstein field equations descend through Lovelock's uniqueness theorem fixed at κ = 8π G/c⁴ by the Newtonian limit. The Schwarzschild solution, gravitational time dilation, redshift, light bending, Mercury's perihelion, transverse-traceless gravitational waves, FLRW cosmology, the Hawking temperature, and the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy S = k_B A/(4ℓ_P²) are all theorems of (ℳ_G, D_M).

On the quantum side, the wavefunction ψ is constructed as the projection of x₄-advance onto x₁ x₂ x₃ on the McGucken Sphere. The complex character of ψ is forced by the imaginary character of x₄ = ic t. The canonical commutation relation [q̂, p̂] = iℏ is forced through the Minkowski metric and four-momentum as generator of translations. The Hilbert space ℋ = L²(M_{1,3}, dμ_M) is the Cauchy completion of square-integrable amplitudes via Riesz--Fischer 1907. The Born rule P = |ψ|² is forced by bilinearity of x₄-flux plus phase invariance plus reality plus normalization. The uncertainty principle σₓσₚ ≥ ℏ/2 follows by a McGucken-internal Robertson lemma. The Wick rotation is the McGucken coordinate identification τ = x₄/c.

The category 𝔐 of moving-dimension manifolds with (ℳ_G, D_M) as terminal source-pair completes Klein's 1872 Erlangen Programme: where Klein supplied a mathematical correspondence between geometry and group, the McGucken framework supplies the single physical principle from which both descend as parallel sibling consequences (Channel A: invariance group; Channel B: McGucken Sphere wavefront).

The closure principle is:

    ** dx₄/dt = ic  ⇒  (ℳ_G, D_M)  ⇒  the spaces and operators of fundamental physics.** 

McGucken Space is foundationally maximal in derivability and primitively minimal in source-law count: C(ℳ_G) = 1, the smallest possible nonzero primitive-law complexity. The framework derives both the spaces and the operators of physics from one physical principle, not by quantizing gravity nor by geometrizing quantum mechanics, but by recognizing that the geometry has been there all along, in the physical fact that the fourth dimension is expanding at the velocity of light from every spacetime event.
